```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Global options: hide code, suppress warnings, centre all figures
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo      = FALSE,
  warning   = FALSE,
  message   = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

# Packages
# tidyverse - data wrangling and ggplot2 charts
# scales    - formats numbers with commas and % on axes
# knitr + kableExtra - for PDF-friendly tables (same as KCSE report)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```

```{r load-revenue-data, include=FALSE}
# Revenue figures are built here (hidden) so summary statistics are available
# for the Executive Summary below. The same code is shown, for transparency,
# in the "Data Entry" section under Data and Methodology further down.
fy <- 2013:2025

equitable  <- c(
  2.81, 3.53, 3.84, 4.14, 4.1, 4.46,
  4.30, 4.67, 5.13, 5.54, 5.34, 5.80, 6.08
)

own_source <- c(
  0.6591, 0.748, 0.63076, 0.80377, 0.83978, 0.950,
  0.920, 0.93778, 0.900, 0.51414, 0.750, 1.55, 1.36
)

conditional <- c(
  0.5572, 0.01137, 0.42075, 0.51872, 0.74903, 1.10,
  1.26, 0.99806, 0.62812, 0.43586, 1.21, 1.00, 0.98140
)

budget <- data.frame(
  FY          = fy,
  Equitable   = equitable,
  OwnSource   = own_source,
  Conditional = conditional
)

budget$Total_Revenue    <- budget$Equitable + budget$OwnSource + budget$Conditional
budget$OSR_Pct          <- round(budget$OwnSource   / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
budget$Equitable_Pct    <- round(budget$Equitable   / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
budget$Conditional_Pct  <- round(budget$Conditional / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
```

\newpage

# Executive Summary

This report presents an analysis of Embu County budget allocations from
**FY 2013/14 to FY 2025/26**. All monetary figures are expressed in **KES
Billions** unless otherwise stated. The analysis covers four key areas:

- **Equitable Share** — national transfers to the county
- **Own Source Revenue (OSR)** — locally collected revenue
- **Conditional Allocations** — grants tied to specific programmes
- **Departmental Allocations** — how the budget is distributed across sectors

Data was sourced from the Office of the Controller of Budget Annual County
Budget Implementation Reports.

```{r summary-numbers, include=FALSE}
# Key summary statistics used throughout the report (Executive Summary and
# Conclusions). Calculated early, right after the data is assembled, so both
# sections stay in sync with the underlying figures.
avg_osr_pct       <- round(mean(budget$OSR_Pct,       na.rm = TRUE), 1)
avg_equitable_pct <- round(mean(budget$Equitable_Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
revenue_cagr       <- round((
  (budget$Total_Revenue[budget$FY == max(budget$FY)] /
     budget$Total_Revenue[budget$FY == min(budget$FY)]
  )^(1 / (max(budget$FY) - min(budget$FY))) - 1
) * 100, 1)
```

**Key figures at a glance:** over the period reviewed, Equitable Share has
averaged **`r avg_equitable_pct`%** of total county revenue, while Own Source
Revenue has averaged only **`r avg_osr_pct`%** — well below the 15% national
target. Total revenue has grown at a compound annual rate of roughly
**`r revenue_cagr`%** over the thirteen financial years covered.

\newpage

# Data and Methodology

## Data Entry

Figures below are annual totals in **KES Billions**, by financial year
(FY 2013/14 through FY 2025/26). The code is shown here for transparency;
it was already run earlier (see the hidden `load-revenue-data` chunk) so
that summary statistics could feed into the Executive Summary above.

```{r data-listing, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
fy <- 2013:2025

# Equitable Share, Own Source Revenue, and Conditional Allocations,
# one value per financial year, in KES Billions
equitable  <- c(
  2.81, 3.53, 3.84, 4.14, 4.1, 4.46,
  4.30, 4.67, 5.13, 5.54, 5.34, 5.80, 6.08
)

own_source <- c(
  0.6591, 0.748, 0.63076, 0.80377, 0.83978, 0.950,
  0.920, 0.93778, 0.900, 0.51414, 0.750, 1.55, 1.36
)

conditional <- c(
  0.5572, 0.01137, 0.42075, 0.51872, 0.74903, 1.10,
  1.26, 0.99806, 0.62812, 0.43586, 1.21, 1.00, 0.98140
)

# Build the main revenue data frame and derive totals / percentage shares
budget <- data.frame(
  FY          = fy,
  Equitable   = equitable,
  OwnSource   = own_source,
  Conditional = conditional
)

budget$Total_Revenue   <- budget$Equitable + budget$OwnSource + budget$Conditional
budget$OSR_Pct         <- round(budget$OwnSource   / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
budget$Equitable_Pct   <- round(budget$Equitable   / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
budget$Conditional_Pct <- round(budget$Conditional / budget$Total_Revenue * 100, 1)
```

Departmental allocations are shown for the six sectors with complete data
across all thirteen financial years. An "Other" category was considered but
dropped here since no reliable figures were available for it; `Total_Dept`
below therefore represents the sum of these six tracked sectors, not the
full county budget.

```{r dept-data, echo=TRUE}
departments <- data.frame(
  FY              = fy,
  Health          = c(0.276,  0.36638,  1.37056, 1.61719,  1.58212,
                      1.92910,  1.91012,  2.0371,  1.87249,
                       1.80832,  1.91254,  1.37007, 1.76699),

  Education       = c(0.045,  0.01386,  0.14554,  0.37349,  0.33967,
                      0.43738, 0.38055,  0.3041,  0.43913,
                      0.42928, 0.380,  0.39510, 0.45075),

  County_Assembly = c(0.484, 0.41676, 0.48431,  0.50366, 0.50812,
                      0.59274,  0.59252,  0.683,  0.69907,
                      0.84795,  0.624,  0.74508, 0.654),

  Roads           = c(0.014, 0.03509,  0.06428,  0.06552, 0.05911,
                      0.06832, 0.06464,  0.0600,  0.05640,
                      0.04588, 0.039, 0.07664, 0.09478),

  Agriculture     = c(0.015,  0.03051, 0.25690,  0.23185, 0.25188,
                      0.37928, 0.27228, 0.3692, 0.40839,
                      0.25593, 0.290, 0.27546, 0.22873),

  Public_Admin    = c(0.032,  0.0154,  0.23274,  0.31818,  0.26981,
                       0.46845,  0.34762,  0.3978, 0.50096,
                      0.67780, 0.577,  1.00426, 0.93242)
)

# Row-wise total across the six tracked departments (exclude FY column)
departments$Total_Dept <- rowSums(departments[, -1], na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Methodology

Revenue and departmental figures were manually extracted from Controller of
Budget reports. Analysis was conducted in R to compute:

- Year-on-year growth rates
- Revenue composition (% share per stream)
- OSR dependency ratio
- Departmental share of total budget

### Limitations

- Figures were transcribed manually from published PDF reports; transcription
  errors, while checked, cannot be fully ruled out.
- Departmental analysis covers six sectors with complete year-on-year data
  (Health, Education, County Assembly, Roads, Agriculture, Public
  Administration). `Total_Dept` reflects the sum of these six sectors, not
  the county's full departmental budget.
- Figures are nominal (not inflation-adjusted), so year-on-year growth
  partly reflects price inflation rather than real budget expansion.

# Revenue Trend Analysis

## Summary Table

```{r summary-table}
# Display the raw revenue figures in a clean table
# format.args adds comma separators to large numbers
budget[, c("FY", "Equitable",
           "OwnSource", "Conditional", "Total_Revenue")] |>
  kable(
    booktabs    = TRUE,
    caption     = "Revenue Performance by Financial Year (KES Billions)",
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2),
    col.names   = c("FY", "Equitable Share", "Own Source Revenue",
                    "Conditional Allocations", "Total Revenue"),
    align       = "lrrrr"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Year-on-Year Growth Rate

```{r growth-table}
# Compute how much Total Revenue grew from one year to the next
# diff() gives the change; dividing by the prior year gives the growth rate
growth <- c(NA, round(diff(budget$Total_Revenue) / head(budget$Total_Revenue, -1) * 100, 1))

growth_table <- data.frame(
  FY            = budget$FY,
  Total_Revenue = budget$Total_Revenue,
  `Growth %`    = growth,
  check.names   = FALSE
)

kable(
  growth_table,
  booktabs    = TRUE,
  caption     = "Year-on-Year Total Revenue Growth (KES Billions)",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2),
  align       = "lrr"
) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Revenue Trend Chart

```{r trend-plot, fig.cap="Trend of Major Revenue Streams (2013-2025)"}
# Reshape to long format so we can colour by revenue stream
# Each row becomes: FY | Revenue_Type | Amount
budget_long <- reshape(
  budget[, c("FY", "Equitable", "OwnSource", "Conditional")],
  idvar     = "FY",
  varying   = c("Equitable", "OwnSource", "Conditional"),
  v.names   = "Amount",
  timevar   = "Revenue_Type",
  times     = c("Equitable Share", "Own Source Revenue", "Conditional"),
  direction = "long"
)

# Colour palette matching the report style
pal_revenue <- c(
  "Equitable Share"    = "#2980b9",
  "Own Source Revenue" = "#c0392b",
  "Conditional"        = "#27ae60"
)

ggplot(budget_long, aes(x = FY, y = Amount, colour = Revenue_Type, group = Revenue_Type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = fy) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_revenue, name = "") +
  labs(
    title   = "Embu County Revenue Streams (FY 2013/14 to 2025/26)",
    x       = "Financial Year",
    y       = "Amount (KES Billions)",
    caption = "Source: Controller of Budget Annual Reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    # Angle x-axis labels so years don't overlap
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### Observation

Equitable share shows a steady upward trend in line with the Commission on
Revenue Allocation (CRA) vertical revenue sharing formula. Own Source Revenue
has remained relatively stagnant, indicating a need for revenue enhancement
measures at the county level.

# Budget Composition and Dependency

## Revenue Composition Over Time

```{r composition, fig.cap="Revenue Composition Over Time (100% Stacked Area)"}
# 100% stacked area chart — shows the SHARE of each revenue stream per year
# regardless of how total revenue has grown
budget_pct <- reshape(
  budget[, c("FY", "Equitable_Pct", "OSR_Pct", "Conditional_Pct")],
  idvar     = "FY",
  varying   = c("Equitable_Pct", "OSR_Pct", "Conditional_Pct"),
  v.names   = "Percent",
  timevar   = "Revenue_Type",
  times     = c("Equitable Share", "Own Source Revenue", "Conditional"),
  direction = "long"
)

ggplot(budget_pct, aes(x = FY, y = Percent, fill = Revenue_Type)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = fy) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_revenue, name = "") +
  labs(
    title   = "Revenue Composition — Percentage Share per Year",
    x       = "Financial Year",
    y       = "% of Total Revenue",
    caption = "Source: Controller of Budget Annual Reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## OSR Dependency Table

```{r osr-table}
# OSR dependency = Own Source Revenue as a % of Total Revenue
# A low % means the county relies heavily on national transfers
osr_table <- data.frame(
  FY            = budget$FY,
  OwnSource     = budget$OwnSource,
  Total_Revenue = budget$Total_Revenue,
  `OSR %`       = budget$OSR_Pct,
  check.names   = FALSE
)

kable(
  osr_table,
  booktabs    = TRUE,
  caption     = "Own Source Revenue (OSR) Dependency Ratio",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2),
  col.names   = c("FY", "Own Source Revenue (KES Bn)", "Total Revenue (KES Bn)", "OSR as % of Total"),
  align       = "lrrr"
) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) |>
  # Highlight the OSR % column to draw the reader's attention
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE)
```

## OSR Trend Chart

```{r osr-chart, fig.cap="Own Source Revenue Dependency Ratio Over Time", fig.height=4}
# Bar chart showing OSR % each year with a reference line at 15%
# (the national target for county OSR contribution)
ggplot(budget, aes(x = factor(FY), y = OSR_Pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#c0392b", width = 0.65) +
  # Dashed reference line at the 15% national target
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 16, label = "15% target",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title   = "OSR as % of Total Revenue per Year",
    x       = "Financial Year",
    y       = "OSR %",
    caption = "Source: Controller of Budget Annual Reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

### Observation

The county's OSR contribution has remained below the national target of 15%.
This heavy reliance on equitable share exposes the county to delays in national
revenue disbursements and limits fiscal autonomy.

# Departmental Allocation Analysis

## Departmental Allocations Over Time

```{r dept-plot, fig.cap="Departmental Budget Allocations Over Time (Stacked Area)"}
# Reshape departments to long format for plotting
# Each row becomes: FY | Department | Allocation
dept_long <- reshape(
  departments[, names(departments) != "Total_Dept"],
  idvar     = "FY",
  varying   = c("Health", "Education", "County_Assembly",
                "Roads", "Agriculture", "Public_Admin"),
  v.names   = "Allocation",
  timevar   = "Department",
  times     = c("Health", "Education", "County Assembly",
                "Roads", "Agriculture", "Public Admin"),
  direction = "long"
)

pal_dept <- c(
  "Health"          = "#2980b9",
  "Education"       = "#27ae60",
  "County Assembly" = "#8e44ad",
  "Roads"           = "#e67e22",
  "Agriculture"     = "#16a085",
  "Public Admin"    = "#c0392b"
)

ggplot(dept_long, aes(x = FY, y = Allocation, fill = Department)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = fy) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_dept, name = "") +
  labs(
    title   = "Departmental Budget Allocations (FY 2013/14 to 2025/26)",
    x       = "Financial Year",
    y       = "Allocation (KES Billions)",
    caption = "Source: Controller of Budget Annual Reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## Department Shares — Latest Financial Year

```{r dept-latest}
# Filter to the most recent year and rank departments by allocation
latest_fy  <- max(departments$FY)
latest_row <- departments[departments$FY == latest_fy, ]
total_dept <- latest_row$Total_Dept

# Build a ranked summary table for the latest FY
dept_names <- c("Health", "Education", "County_Assembly",
                "Roads", "Agriculture", "Public_Admin")

dept_values <- as.numeric(latest_row[, dept_names])

latest_table <- data.frame(
  Department = c("Health", "Education", "County Assembly",
                 "Roads", "Agriculture", "Public Admin"),
  Allocation = dept_values,
  Share_Pct  = round(dept_values / total_dept * 100, 1)
)

# Sort by largest allocation first
latest_table <- latest_table[order(-latest_table$Allocation), ]

kable(
  latest_table,
  booktabs    = TRUE,
  caption     = paste("Departmental Allocation Ranking — FY", latest_fy, "/", latest_fy + 1,
                       "(KES Billions)"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2),
  col.names   = c("Department", "Allocation (KES Bn)", "Share (%)"),
  align       = "lrr",
  row.names   = FALSE
) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) |>
  column_spec(3, bold = TRUE)
```

## Department Allocation Bar Chart — Latest Year

```{r dept-bar, fig.cap="Department Allocation Ranking — Latest Financial Year", fig.height=4}
# Horizontal bar chart makes department names easy to read
ggplot(latest_table, aes(x = reorder(Department, Allocation), y = Allocation, fill = Department)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Add % share label at the end of each bar
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Share_Pct, "%")), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip() +   # flip so departments are on the y-axis
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_dept) +
  labs(
    title   = paste("Department Allocation Ranking — FY", latest_fy),
    x       = "",
    y       = "Allocation (KES Billions)",
    caption = "Source: Controller of Budget Annual Reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

# Conclusions and Recommendations

```{r conclusion-numbers, include=FALSE}
# avg_osr_pct and avg_equitable_pct were already computed in the
# load-revenue-data / summary-numbers chunks near the top of the report.
# Only the Health + Roads share (needs latest_table, built later) is new here.
health_roads_alloc <- sum(latest_table$Allocation[latest_table$Department %in% c("Health", "Roads")])
health_roads_pct   <- round(health_roads_alloc / total_dept * 100, 1)
```

## Conclusions

1. **Revenue Dependency** — Embu County relies on equitable share for an average
   of **`r avg_equitable_pct`%** of its total revenue, exposing it to fiscal
   risks from delayed national disbursements.

2. **OSR Underperformance** — Own Source Revenue averages **`r avg_osr_pct`%**
   of total revenue, well below the 15% national target. This signals
   underutilised local revenue potential.

3. **Departmental Priority** — Health and Roads combined account for
   **`r health_roads_pct`%** of the total department budget in
   FY `r latest_fy`/`r latest_fy + 1`, reflecting the county's focus on
   basic services and infrastructure.

4. **Steady Revenue Growth** — Total county revenue has grown at a compound
   annual rate of roughly **`r revenue_cagr`%** over the analysis period,
   driven primarily by increases in equitable share transfers from the
   national government.

## Recommendations

- **Strengthen OSR collection** — The county should review its revenue streams
  (business licences, land rates, market fees) and invest in collection
  mechanisms to approach the 15% OSR target.

- **Diversify revenue sources** — Reducing dependence on equitable share would
  improve fiscal resilience, especially during periods of delayed national
  disbursements.

- **Maintain health and infrastructure investment** — The prioritisation of
  Health and Roads should be sustained and, where possible, increased to
  support service delivery targets.

- **Improve budget absorption** — Future analysis should compare allocated
  versus actual expenditure to assess implementation efficiency.
